- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.65) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤0.35), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for risk reversal.
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above peak for next 3–5 periods.
- If sentiment shows strong reversal (e.g., from +0.7 to -0.4), model lags in adjusting; shift forecast downward by 2–5% in next 2–4 periods.
- Mean reversion is evident when forecast deviates >5% from 10-day moving average; pull forecast toward average within 3–5 periods.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overfits recent volatility; dampen forecast by 1–2% if sentiment is neutral or mildly positive.
